International public-market mapping is incomplete, especially Canada, India, Japan, Korea, Europe, Australia, and listed suppliers to transformer OEMs and HVDC projects.
Nuclear fuel-cycle exposure is still dominated by limited or diluted public mappings; conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and advanced fuel fabrication require more primary-source verification.

Customer/supplier dependency maps are preliminary; next checks should include customer concentration, approved-vendor status, backlog timing, lead times, capacity additions, and margin sensitivity to copper, steel, uranium, and labor costs.

memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1 universe currently has strongest investable evidence in grid and power-delivery hardware rather than in broad commodity energy exposure.
Transmission-line hardware, utility structures, dry-type transformers, power-quality products, and HVDC transformer inputs should remain priority nodes for Layer 2 validation.
Nuclear conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and advanced fuel fabrication may be tighter bottlenecks than uranium mining, but listed pure-play exposure is limited or diluted.
Energy universe remains too narrow without a dedicated oil and gas infrastructure pass covering LNG, turbines, compression, pipelines, backup generation, and field electrification.

Layer 2 should upgrade secondary research evidence with primary filings, earnings-call transcripts, investor presentations, utility procurement records, regulatory filings, and qualified-vendor lists.

summary: Layer 1C merged the available Layer 1A theme map and visible Layer 1B node-level candidates into an initial Energy universe ranked by Serenity relevance. The strongest current cluster is grid and power-delivery hardware: transmission-line fittings, utility structures, dry-type transformers, power-quality equipment, HVDC transformer inputs, and downstream T&D construction validation. Nuclear fuel-cycle names are included mainly as reference or constrained public-market mappings because the tightest nodes, especially conversion and advanced fuel fabrication, have limited pure-play public exposure. The universe remains narrow in oil and gas infrastructure, LNG, compression, turbines, storage, inverters, and international electrical-equipment suppliers, which should be expanded in the next pass.
